Modules, data and pseudocode

Unit 1 · Week 8 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the brief, schedule, workbook section 3 and unfinished project-starter.py. Prepare paper for a structure chart. No finished project solution is required.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Modules, data and pseudocode

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means divide responsibilities between modules, specify their inputs/results/side effects, agree data representations and describe the mainline algorithm. Students design their own implementation using the existing chapter brief.

2. Retrieval: functions and interfaces

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and partner explanation

A parameter receives a supplied argument. return provides a result to the caller, whereas print displays output. Isolating order_cost lets us test without keyboard input or file changes. A structure chart shows module calls rather than every branch and loop. Use this as a diagnostic before presenting the chapter module names.

3. A structure chart shows calls

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked structure chart and verbal rehearsal

The indented tree represents the chapter’s structure chart: main coordinates all five subordinate modules. Box and connect the names on paper if preferred. It shows call relationships, not chronological control flow or a flowchart. main repeats the order steps and later requests the summary. Ask students to explain one responsibility and add input/result labels to their own chart.

4. An interface is an agreement

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked contract and paired completion

read_order_id returns a valid invented label; read_quantity returns a valid integer >= 0. order_cost(quantity) returns integer cents and does no file or keyboard I/O. save_order receives ID, quantity and cost and appends one record; agree a failure signal with main. summarise_orders receives the quantity list and reports or returns a documented summary; choose and record a consistent interface. Table contains selected examples, not every module. Students complete all interfaces including side effects.

5. The data contract

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided design and peer explanation

The record example represents synthetic ID A01, quantity 2 and cost 600 cents. Append a newline after each record. IDs must be non-empty and contain no commas or line breaks. Session list [2,0,5] contains quantities from this run only. Use integer cents to avoid floating-point currency calculations. Decide who validates each field. Discuss the dependency: save successfully before adding to the session list, otherwise session totals could include an unsaved order.

6. Mainline pseudocode

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired algorithm design and role change

This is language-neutral pseudocode, not runnable Python. Fill the SAVE failure policy explicitly: display failure and offer retry/cancel, without claiming a saved order or adding a quantity prematurely. Do not silently skip validation. Students annotate the loop, selection, function calls and data movement then write their own detailed algorithm and interfaces. Swap explainer/checker roles halfway. Support: use chapter pseudocode. Extension: show how a cancelled retry returns to the organiser menu.

7. A stub exposes unfinished work

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict and explain

Calling this stub raises NotImplementedError and saves no file. It marks a deliberate placeholder, not a working save operation. Students compare this to a pass stub that might silently do nothing. They can inspect project-starter.py but should not run the whole unfinished program expecting success. Replace and test stubs in later build lessons.

8. Checkpoint: a connected design

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket and partner handover

Students retain a structure chart, every interface contract, list/file data description and mainline pseudocode. A peer should identify which module supplies each value and how failure reaches the caller. Expected one clear job per function, explicit side effects, current-session versus persistent storage distinction. Collect any unresolved failure policy for lesson 4 review.
